name: Accessibility ramp
description: Wooden ramp with optional switchback, landings, curbs and handrails.

params_schema.description:
Ramp parameters. Bounds not stated in the original spec were inferred: available_length_in, slope_ratio,
landing_length_in, stringer_spacing_in and deck_gap_in.

Schema hints for the parameter panel (in `json_schema_extra`): `group` is "key" for the few dimensions
a homeowner measures and "advanced" for construction choices, which the panel folds away;
`enum_labels` gives readable names for the choices; `unit` is the unit of a number.

total_rise_in.description: From the ground to the top of the porch or doorway, measured straight up. Three standard steps are about 21 in.
total_rise_in.title: Rise (height to climb)

clear_width_in.description: Walking width of the whole ramp, edge to edge inside the curbs. Every run and landing gets this width; 36 in fits a wheelchair.
clear_width_in.title: Ramp width

available_length_in.description: How far the yard extends out from the porch. Leave empty if space isn't a limit; if a straight ramp won't fit, Chisel suggests a switchback.
available_length_in.title: Space in front (optional)

layout.description: Automatic uses a straight ramp when it fits the space and the lumber, otherwise a switchback (two runs side by side with a turn landing).
layout.title: Layout

slope_ratio.description: 12 means 1:12, the usual guideline for wheelchairs; higher is gentler and longer.
slope_ratio.title: Slope (inches of ramp per inch of rise)

landing_length_in.description: Length of each flat landing between runs, where people rest or turn.
landing_length_in.title: Landing length

framing.description: Boards for the stringers (the sloped supports) and the landing frames.
framing.title: Framing lumber

stringer_spacing_in.description: Distance between the sloped supports under the deck, center to center. Closer is stiffer.
stringer_spacing_in.title: Stringer spacing

deck_gap_in.description: Gap between deck boards for drainage.
deck_gap_in.title: Deck board gap

handrails.description: Automatic adds handrails on both sides when the rise needs them.
handrails.title: Handrails

edge_curb.description: A 2x6 curb along the open sides so wheels and canes can't slip off the edge.
edge_curb.title: Edge curb

params_schema.title: Params

name: Raised garden bed
description: Raised garden bed with stacked side boards, corner posts and an optional seat-height cap rail.

params_schema.description:
Garden bed parameters. Bounds inferred (not in the original spec): width_in and height_in, and
length_in, whose 144 in maximum is the longest 2x10 sold so the long sides stay single boards.

Schema hints for the parameter panel are the same as the ramp's: `group` ("key" or "advanced"),
`enum_labels` and `unit`.

length_in.description: Outside length of the bed, end to end along the long sides. The long sides are single boards, so 12 ft is the most.
length_in.title: Length

width_in.description: Outside width of the bed, from the front face to the back face. Keep it within reach: about 24 in from one side, 48 in from both.
width_in.title: Width

height_in.description: From the ground to the very top of the bed, including the cap rail when there is one.
height_in.title: Height

access.description: Which long sides you can stand at to work the bed. It sets how wide the bed can be and still be reached.
access.title: Reach from

board.description: Lumber stacked on edge to make the walls. The top course is ripped narrower when the height isn't a whole number of boards.
board.title: Side boards

cap_rail.description: A flat 2x6 rail around the top edge that doubles as a seat or armrest. It counts toward the height.
cap_rail.title: Cap rail

params_schema.title: Params

name: Step platform
description: Wooden steps up to a porch, with notched stringers, deck-board treads and risers.

params_schema.description:
Step platform parameters. Bounds not stated in the original spec were inferred: width_in,
tread_depth_in, max_riser_in and step_count.

Schema hints for the parameter panel (see `ramp.Params`): `group` "key" for what a homeowner measures
or decides, "advanced" for construction choices; `unit` is the unit of a number; `empty_label` is
what an empty optional value means (the panel says "No limit" without it).

total_rise_in.description: From the ground to the top of the porch or doorway, measured straight up. The top step is the porch itself.
total_rise_in.title: Rise (height to climb)

width_in.description: Width of every step, from one side edge to the other.
width_in.title: Step width

tread_depth_in.description: How far each step goes back, from the front of one step to the front of the next. 11 in is the usual minimum.
tread_depth_in.title: Step depth

max_riser_in.description: The most any one step may rise, top of one step to the top of the next. Sets how many steps are built when the number of steps is left empty.
max_riser_in.title: Tallest step allowed

step_count.description: How many times you step up, counting the step onto the porch. Leave empty for the fewest steps that keep each riser under the tallest step allowed.
step_count.title: Number of steps

params_schema.title: Params

name: Workbench
description: Workbench with 4x4 legs, 2x4 aprons, a plywood top and an optional lower shelf.

params_schema.description:
Workbench parameters. All bounds are inferred (the spec gave sizes, not limits): the width and depth
stop at one 48 x 96 in plywood sheet because the top is a single piece.

Schema hints for the parameter panel (in `json_schema_extra`), as on the ramp: `group` is "key" for the
overall size a homeowner decides and "advanced" for construction choices, which the panel folds away;
`unit` is the unit of a number.

width_in.description: Length of the top from left to right, edge to edge. The top is one piece of plywood, so it can be at most 96 in (the long side of a sheet).
width_in.title: Width

depth_in.description: Size of the top from front to back, edge to edge. It can be at most 48 in (the short side of a plywood sheet).
depth_in.title: Depth

height_in.description: From the floor to the top of the work surface, measured straight up.
height_in.title: Working-surface height

lower_shelf.description: A plywood shelf between the legs, resting on 2x4 supports, with its top surface 10 in above the floor.
lower_shelf.title: Lower shelf
